raw:
I remember a child in the park looking for a lost mitten. They had one bare hand tucked inside their sleeve, and that was what caught my attention. It made me feel sorry for them—trying to look for something while keeping that hand covered.

I helped check beneath the park benches. It was a small thing to do, but I wanted to help rather than just walk past. What stayed with me was that bare hand tucked away in the sleeve. I don’t remember whether we found the mitten, but I remember feeling that losing something so ordinary could be a big thing for that child at that moment.
